# Tabs

Navigate through different pages or sections that have the same context.
See [Tab guidelines<i className="ds-icon-launch"></i>](https://design-system.airbus.corp/components/tab/design/)

<Source code="import { Tab, Tabs } from &#x22;@airbus/components-react&#x22;" />

<Primary />

<Controls />

- Any other props supplied will be provided to the `<ul>` and `<li>` HTML elements
- For details on CSS styles, see [CSS implementation](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system/blob/develop/packages/styles/src/elements/Tabs/index.ts)

### Links

Provide an `href` prop to allow users to copy link or open in new tab.

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Links} />

### Floating

Floating option can be used to make the tabs visually float, without the bottom border line.

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Floating} />

### Scrolling

On desktop when space is too limited to display a large amount of tabs, we recommend using a Menu instead.<br />
On Touch devices, you can use the `scrollable` prop to allow user agent scrolling mechanisms (e.g. left/right swipe, shift-mousewheel, etc.)

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Scrolling} />

### React-router

Here is an example with the popular [react-router](https://reactrouter.com/en/main/start/tutorial) library.<br />

- React router `useLocation` hook provide the current `location.pathname`
- React router `Link` component can be used with the `Tab` `component` prop

```js static
import { Link, useLocation, Outlet, RouterProvider, createBrowserRouter } from "react-router-dom";
import { Tabs, Tab } from "@airbus/components-react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

const SampleHeader = () => {
  const location = useLocation();
  return (
    <>
    <header>
      <Tabs value={location.pathname}>
          <Tab component={Link} to="/page1" value="/page1">
            Page 1
          </Tab>
          <Tab component={Link} to="/page2" value="/page2">
            Page 2
          </Tab>
          <Tab component={Link} to="/page3" value="/page3">
            Page 3
          </Tab>
      </Tabs>
    </header>
    </>
  );
};

const router = createBrowserRouter([
  {
    path: "/",
    element: (
      <>
        <SampleHeader />
        <Outlet />
      </>
    ),
    children: [
      {
        path: "/page1",
        element: <h1>Page 1</h1>
      },
      {
        path: "/page2",
        element: <h1>Page 2</h1>
      },
      {
        path: "/page3",
        element: <h1>Page 3</h1>
      }
    ]
  }
]);

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(<RouterProvider router={router} />);
```
